newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber generally lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber generally lower in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade March SIR20 offer prices were generally lower in lethargic late trading on Wednesday after an absence of buyers, traders said.

They said SIR20 was easier at 54.25 U.S. cents/lb against morning's price of 54.25-54.50 fob Palembang. In Padang, offer prices were unchanged at 54.00 U.S. cents/lb but levels fell 0.25 U.S. cents to 54.50 fob Medan and Surabaya.

Traders said offer prices were unchanged in Pontianak and Jambi at 53.75 U.S. cents/lb. "Offer prices are generally lower as there are no buyers. Traders lifted the price yesterday, but it was useless in the absence of buyers," said one trader.

Traders said they might have to end up selling at a low price due to the absence of buyers. Regional traders have said weak demand from major consumers in Europe, the U.S. and Japan will curtail the upside potential for prices in the coming week.
Some Indonesian traders said the fall in the local market was not necessary caused by the drop in Tokyo.
"The main problem is the absence of buyers. You know it will be useless if prices go up in Tokyo, for instance, as there are no buyers," said one trader.
Tokyo rubber futures ended lower across the board on Wednesday, depressed by the yen's rise against the dollar.
Traders said foreign buyers were taking a wait-and-see stance hoping Indonesia prices will ease.
They also said supply started to improve locally because farmers had returned to work after celebrating the Eid al-Fitr Moslem holiday on February 9 and 10.
